name: Endometrial (uterine) cancer
theme: the molecular reclassification · the dMMR-IO era

meta.title: Endometrial cancer in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Endometrial carcinoma (endometrioid, serous, clear-cell, carcinosarcoma), adult
meta.population: Adults with endometrial carcinoma - the disease the MOLECULAR RECLASSIFICATION rebuilt: TCGA's four groups (POLE-ultramutated / dMMR / p53-abnormal / NSMP), made clinic-ready by ProMisE and now embedded in FIGO staging itself, route adjuvant therapy more powerfully than anatomic stage - and 2025-26 delivered the receipts in both directions: PORTEC-4a proved molecular-directed DE-escalation safe (sparing roughly half of favorable-profile women radiotherapy), while KEYNOTE-B21 proved the 1L immunotherapy benefit does NOT simply port to adjuvant all-comers. Carcinosarcoma rides inside (a high-grade metaplastic carcinoma, treated as high-risk carcinoma - the 1L IO trials enrolled it); uterine SARCOMAS (leiomyosarcoma, ESS) are a different disease and reroute. The advanced-disease story is the dMMR-IO era: two chemo-immunotherapy regimens approved for all comers, with the benefit spectacular in dMMR disease (RUBY: OS HR 0.32, four-year data carrying curative-intent language) and honest-thinner in pMMR.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for the disease where a pathology report reroutes more therapy than a scan. The reclassification is the core: PORTEC-3's molecular reanalysis showed p53-abnormal disease draws nearly all the benefit from added chemotherapy (5-yr RFS 48% - the group that needs more) while POLE-mutant disease runs 98% relapse-free REGARDLESS of adjuvant therapy (the group that may need nothing) - and PORTEC-4a then randomized molecular-directed de-escalation and WON its non-inferiority (2025-26, verified: half of favorable-profile women safely spared radiotherapy). The adjuv…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic teaching environment. Not medical advice; every number is a claim with a citation and an expiry date.
meta.classification: FIGO 2023 (molecular classes embedded); the TCGA/ProMisE four-group system (POLEmut / dMMR / p53abn / NSMP) as the operative router; universal MMR IHC on every carcinoma (the Lynch cascade's front door); NCCN Uterine v3.2026 (secondhand - 403)
meta.response: RECIST 1.1 for advanced disease; the adjuvant era's load-bearing read is the MOLECULAR GROUP itself - a pathology-report line that outranks stage in routing therapy

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A disease of the early 60s, rising with the obesity epidemic; the comorbidity conversation (surgical fitness, competing mortality) often outweighs age itself.
Patient.helpPatient: Overall health shapes these choices more than the birthday - this disease often travels with others.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Routes surgical approach (minimally invasive preferred) and chemo-IO tolerance; obesity and diabetes ride along as the disease's usual companions.
Patient.helpPatient: Fitness shapes the surgery type and treatment intensity.

Disease.label: Histology
Disease.help: Carcinosarcoma stays HERE - reclassified as a high-grade metaplastic carcinoma, treated as high-risk carcinoma (the 1L IO trials enrolled it). Leiomyosarcoma and the other true sarcomas are a differe…
Disease.helpPatient: The microscope sorts two different diseases that share an organ - and one rare mixed type belongs with the more common one, on purpose.

Disease.label: Stage (the fork)
Disease.help: FIGO 2023 - the staging system that embedded the molecular classes into itself: the trainer's fork is anatomic, but the adjuvant router is molecular, and the 2023 revision made that official.
Disease.helpPatient: How far the cancer has traveled picks the menu - and within the early menu, the tumor's molecular type picks the treatment.

Disease.label: Molecular group (the router)
Disease.help: The TCGA four-group system, clinic-ready via ProMisE and embedded in FIGO 2023: it routes the adjuvant menu (the cards hide until it results - a menu routed before its router is known would be dishon…
Disease.helpPatient: A tumor test sorts this cancer into four types with very different behavior - one so favorable that skipping treatment is now a proven option, one that responds unusually well to immunotherapy, one t…

Advanced routing.label: HER2 (serous/p53abn lane)
Advanced routing.help: Tested on serous histology (the p53abn family's usual face): trastuzumab + chemo improved outcomes in HER2+ serous carcinoma (randomized phase 2), T-DXd holds the pan-tumor IHC3+ door, and NRG-GY026…
Advanced routing.helpPatient: One more tumor test on the aggressive type can open an antibody lane borrowed from breast-cancer medicine.

Advanced routing.label: Prior immunotherapy exposure
Advanced routing.help: The 1L chemo-IO era created a population its own 2L evidence never enrolled: KEYNOTE-775 randomized mostly IO-naive patients, so post-IO relapse is honestly evidence-thin - the trial door (MK-2870-00…
Advanced routing.helpPatient: Whether immunotherapy was already used changes how well the next options are proven - for the newest situation, a major trial is asking the question directly.

On treatment.label: Surveillance read
On treatment.help: Surveillance runs on exams and symptoms (vaginal-vault recurrence is the classic catch - examinable, often salvageable); imaging on suspicion. The Lynch-cascade job rides the same checkpoint.
On treatment.helpPatient: Follow-up here leans on exams and symptoms - and any bleeding after treatment is always worth a same-week call.

Newly diagnosed.name: Hysterectomy + sentinel-node mapping (the anchor)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the universal early-stage anchor (NCCN secondhand; PDQ live)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: surgical standard + PORTEC-1/2 adjuvant logic (framing); survival figure flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: a usually-minimally-invasive operation; the sentinel-node dividend is the lymphedema mostly not caused
Newly diagnosed.patient: The foundation: removing the uterus with a lymph-node mapping technique that spares most of the old node-surgery's leg-swelling - cures most early disease by itself.

Newly diagnosed.name: POLE-mutant: observation (the de-escalation card, now RCT-backed)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: PDQ itself notes POLE-ultramutated 'adjuvant therapies are avoided' (live); PORTEC-4a the RCT receipt
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 non-inferiority (PORTEC-4a, verified) + the PORTEC-3 molecular reanalysis - labeled (RFS-grade)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none - that is the card's entire content, and it is evidence, not neglect
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the tumor carries the POLE mutation: the proven answer after surgery is often NO further treatment - this type almost never returns, treated or not, and a randomized trial confirmed that skipping radiation is safe.

Newly diagnosed.name: dMMR: radiotherapy without chemotherapy (and the Lynch cascade)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: molecular-routed adjuvant standard (NCCN secondhand); GY020 the open IO question
Newly diagnosed.evidence: PORTEC-3 molecular reanalysis (verified) - labeled (RFS-grade); the adjuvant-IO question honestly open
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: radiotherapy's pelvic ledger - without the chemotherapy the reanalysis showed adds nothing here
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the tumor is mismatch-repair deficient: radiation without chemotherapy is the honest standard (the chemo added nothing in this type) - and the same test result starts a family-screening conversation, because this type can signal an inherited syndrome.
drugs: Adjuvant RT (brachytherapy or EBRT per risk)

Newly diagnosed.name: p53-abnormal: chemoradiation (the group that needs more)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: PORTEC-3 + its molecular reanalysis (verified; 10-yr update PMID flagged) - labeled (RFS-grade)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the full chemoradiation season - justified exactly here, where the reanalysis put the benefit
Newly diagnosed.patient: If the tumor is p53-abnormal: this is the type that genuinely needs the fuller treatment - chemotherapy added to radiation earns its keep here, and essentially only here.

Newly diagnosed.name: Carboplatin-paclitaxel + immunotherapy (RUBY / NRG-GY018 - the 1L era)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: the 1L standard, all-comers (two FDA approvals 2024, secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.evidence: phase 3 randomized x2 (RUBY OS verified incl. 4-yr dMMR; GY018 PFS both cohorts verified) - the median itself flagged
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the platinum-taxane season plus the immune ledger - with the honest counsel that the immunotherapy's biggest wins concentrate in the dMMR type
Newly diagnosed.patient: For spread or returned disease: chemotherapy plus immunotherapy is the new standard for everyone - and for the mismatch-repair-deficient type it works so well that four-year results speak of lasting remissions.

Newly diagnosed.name: Hormonal therapy (the indolent-NSMP lane)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: consensus option for low-grade ER+ indolent disease (PDQ live; NCCN secondhand)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: the gentlest systemic lane in the spec - weight and clot vigilance on progestins
Newly diagnosed.patient: For the slowest-behaving, hormone-sensitive form: hormone tablets can hold the disease for long stretches with the lightest side-effect load on this menu.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: none from therapy; bleeding control is this disease's specific comfort craft
Newly diagnosed.patient: Declining treatment is a real choice, made with the type's honest numbers on the table.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-775 - the pMMR receipt, honestly squeezed)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the pMMR 2L standard (approved; NCCN secondhand) - population honesty carried
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: phase 3 randomized with 5-year maturity (verified) - the era-mismatch honesty attached
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: lenvatinib's ledger leads (hypertension, fatigue, proteinuria) - the dose-holding craft is the skill
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: The proven second-line combination for the mismatch-repair-proficient type: real survival benefit with a demanding tablet - and honest fine print that its trial ran before immunotherapy moved to first line.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Pembrolizumab monotherapy (dMMR 2L - KEYNOTE-158)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the single-agent immune ledger - among the gentler cards here
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For the immune-visible type not yet given immunotherapy: the single immune drug helps half of patients, often durably.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: The HER2 lane (trastuzumab in serous; T-DXd at IHC3+)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: serous-HER2 option (randomized phase 2; T-DXd pan-tumor accelerated - secondhand dates)
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: randomized phase 2 + pan-tumor basket (labeled, never ranked); GY026 the phase 2/3 in flight
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: cardiac surveillance with trastuzumab; the ILD watch with T-DXd - named out loud
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the aggressive type carries the HER2 marker: antibody medicine borrowed from breast cancer genuinely helps - with a stronger drug available at the highest marker level.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: always on the menu, never by drift
Relapsed / recurrent.evidence: teaching estimate (flagged); the subgroup-audit arc and pending shelf carried as notes
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Choosing comfort after the proven lines is a real road - and this card also carries the honest ledger: one hoped-for maintenance drug failed its confirming trial this July, and one promising new drug awaits its full evidence.

Kandoth et al. / TCGA Network: Integrated genomic characterization of endometrial carcinoma - the four groups (POLE ultramutated / MSI hypermutated / copy-number low / copy-number high). Nature 2013;497:67-73 (PMID 23636398, pubmed-url-match)

Talhouk et al. ProMisE: the clinically applicable surrogate (POLE sequencing + MMR IHC + p53 IHC -> POLEmut/dMMR/p53abn/NSMP) - Br J Cancer 2015 (PMID 26172027) + confirmation Cancer 2017 (PMID 28061006), both pubmed-url-matched; the classes now embedded in FIGO 2023
de Boer et al. PORTEC-3: adjuvant chemoradiotherapy vs radiotherapy alone for high-risk endometrial cancer - final results. Lancet Oncol 2018 (PMID 29449189, pubmed-url-match)

Leon-Castillo et al. Molecular classification of PORTEC-3: 5-yr RFS p53abn 48% (essentially ALL the chemo benefit), POLEmut 98% (regardless of therapy), MMRd 72% (no chemo benefit), NSMP 74% - one trial, four verdicts. JCO 2020;38:3388-97 (PMID 32749941, pubmed-url-match; the 10-yr update's PMID resisted matching - FLAGGED, carried via its OS figures qualitatively)

PORTEC-4a (verified): molecular-profile-directed adjuvant therapy for high-intermediate-risk disease - NON-INFERIORITY MET (5-yr vaginal recurrence 4.5% vs 1.6%, upper CI within margin); molecular profiling safely spared ~HALF of favorable-profile women radiotherapy - the first RCT of molecular-integrated-profile-directed adjuvant therapy. Lancet Oncol 2025-26 (PMID 41449145, pubmed-url-match)
RAINBO clinical trial program (design paper): four molecular-class-directed adjuvant trials (p53abn-RED / MMRd-GREEN / NSMP-ORANGE / POLEmut-BLUE). IJGC 2023 (PMID 36600534, pubmed-url-match)

KEYNOTE-B21/ENGOT-en11 (verified anchor PMID 39284383, Ann Oncol): adjuvant pembrolizumab + chemo for high-risk all-comers - DFS NEGATIVE (dMMR-subgroup signal only, trade-coverage verified): the 1L IO benefit did NOT port to adjuvant all-comers - the boundary stone the adjuvant menu renders

Mirza et al. RUBY: dostarlimab + carboplatin-paclitaxel, primary advanced/recurrent EC. NEJM 2023;388:2145-58 (PMID 36972026, pubmed-url-match). FDA: dMMR-only 2023-07-31 -> ALL-COMERS 2024-08-01 (secondhand)
Powell et al. RUBY overall survival: OS HR 0.69 overall (p=0.0020); dMMR/MSI-H HR 0.32; pMMR trend HR 0.79 - the split said exactly. Ann Oncol 2024 (PMID 38866180, pubmed-url-match)
RUBY four-year dMMR survival update: sustained remissions with curative-intent language - the era's deepest tine. (PMID 42215378, pubmed-url-match)

Eskander et al. NRG-GY018/KEYNOTE-868: pembrolizumab + chemo - PFS significantly improved in BOTH separately-powered cohorts (dMMR and pMMR). NEJM 2023;388:2159-70 (PMID 36972022, pubmed-url-match). FDA all-comers 2024-06 (secondhand); the Nat Med 2025 OS update's PMID resisted matching - FLAGGED (dMMR OS clear, pMMR limited, carried qualitatively)

Westin et al. DUO-E: durvalumab + chemo -> maintenance durva +/- olaparib - PFS benefit in both experimental arms (the olaparib add-on effect mainly pMMR). JCO 2024 (PMID 37864337, pubmed-url-match). AtTEnd concordant - its publication PMID resisted THREE match attempts: FLAGGED, not guessed (the named trap class)
O'Malley et al. KEYNOTE-158 (EC cohort): pembrolizumab mono, previously treated MSI-H/dMMR - ORR 50%, durable. JCO 2022 (PMID 34990208, pubmed-url-match)

Makker et al. KEYNOTE-775/Study 309: lenvatinib + pembrolizumab vs chemo (pMMR post-platinum) - OS and PFS superior (primary NEJM 2022 PMID 35045221; final update JCO 2023 PMID 37058687 - both pubmed-url-matched). THE SQUEEZE carried: the trial predates the 1L chemo-IO era
KEYNOTE-775 five-year outcomes: 5-yr OS 16.7% - a real verified tail in a hard population, carried at its exact grade. (PMID 41714113, pubmed-url-match)

THE AUDITED SUBGROUP (the arc, both halves verified at their grades): SIENDO/ENGOT-EN5 failed its ITT primary (PFS 5.7 vs 3.8 NS); the TP53-wild-type signal was EXPLORATORY (JCO exploratory analysis PMID 37669480, matched; XPORT-EC-042 design paper PMID 38627035, matched) - and the confirmation MISSED: XPORT-EC-042 topline 2026-07-30 (mITT mPFS 12.75 vs 7.43, HR 0.76, p=0.0791 one-sided - press-level, publication pending). Selinexor maintenance is NOT a validated standard; the exploratory-signal-meets-audit arc is the lesson

Fader et al. Trastuzumab + carbo-pac in HER2+ uterine serous carcinoma (randomized phase 2): PFS and OS improved - updated-OS paper Clin Cancer Res 2020 (PMID 32601075, pubmed-url-match; the primary's commonly-cited PMID 29584549 NOT matched - FLAGGED, not guessed)

Meric-Bernstam et al. DESTINY-PanTumor02: T-DXd in HER2-expressing solid tumors - the endometrial cohort among the strongest at IHC3+; basis of the 2024-04 tumor-agnostic accelerated approval (secondhand date). JCO 2024 (PMID 37870536, pubmed-url-match; gyn-cohort paper PMID 42135959)

Universal MMR testing + the Lynch cascade (consensus standard: tumor MMR IHC on every EC -> MLH1-methylation reflex -> germline where unexplained -> family cascade); EC is the sentinel cancer in ~half of Lynch women (guideline framing; NCCN wording secondhand)

El-Jawahri A, LeBlanc T, VanDusen H, et al. Effect of Inpatient Palliative Care on Quality of Life 2 Weeks After Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2016;316(20):2094-2103 (PMID 27893130, NCT02207322) — abstract read firsthand 2026-09-10. POPULATION CAUTION, added at that read because the previous label named no population at all: this is a SINGLE-INSTITUTION randomized trial of 160 adults with HAEMATOLOGICAL malignancy hospitalized for autologous or allogeneic stem-cell transplantation, and its outcomes are quality of life, depression, anxiety, fatigue and symptom burden — it reports no survival and no adverse-event table. It is the factory's standing anchor for the PRINCIPLE that palliative care runs alongside active treatment rather than after it; it is not evidence in this tumour type and is not the source of any number on this card.

RAINBO BLUE & TAPER / CCTG EN.10 / NRG-GY032 (NCT05640999): POLEmut (BLUE) and NSMP/p53wt (TAPER) adjuvant DE-ESCALATION, phase 2, 3-yr pelvic recurrence primary - US SITES via NRG-GY032 - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-04-13), registry re-check due. The core RAINBO umbrella (NCT05255653) and RAINBO-RED France (NCT06712472) recruit WITHOUT US sites - named plainly

NRG-GY020 (NCT04214067): vaginal brachytherapy +/- pembrolizumab, dMMR high-intermediate-risk early-stage endometrioid, phase 3, 3-yr RFS primary (NCI/NRG) - WEB-VERIFIED but NO DATED 2026 MIRROR: the screen's HIGHEST re-check priority

TroFuse-033 / GOG-3119 / ENGOT-en29 (NCT06952504): sac-TMT + pembrolizumab vs pembrolizumab alone as 1L MAINTENANCE in pMMR advanced disease, phase 3, 245 locations - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-07), re-check due (primary-endpoint hierarchy unconfirmed)

MK-2870-005 / GOG-3095 / ENGOT-en23 (NCT06132958): sac-TMT vs physician's-choice chemo, POST-PLATINUM AND POST-IO advanced/recurrent EC (carcinosarcoma included), phase 3, OS PRIMARY (~710 pts) - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-03-29), re-check due. Its sibling TroFuse-005's positive topline (2026-05) sits on the pending shelf - press-level, no approval

NRG-GY026 (NCT05256225): carbo-pac +/- trastuzumab(+/-pertuzumab), HER2+ stage I-IVB uterine serous/carcinosarcoma, phase 2/3 seamless (PFS -> OS), wide NRG footprint - WEB-VERIFIED 2026-08 (cache 2026-04-02), re-check due.
